Subject: Follow-up: cost targets & quick competitive signal

Ethan / Asha — thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap and three asks so we can model a proposal by EOW: 

Recap (from our side)
- Volume profile: 20M tokens/month (steady) with spikes to ~60M for monthly reporting windows.
- Primary model class: instruction-tuned open models for summarization + classification (low to medium context lengths).
- Key constraints: sub-100ms p50 latency for synchronous API calls; SOC2 required; procurement wants an O(1–3) month pilot before committing to dedicated.

Cost signals we discussed (rough market context)
- OpenAI (managed): typically higher per-1M for advanced models — often tens to low hundreds $/1M depending on model class.
- Anthropic (hosted): mid-range for their Claude family; varies by model and context length.
- Open-model hosts / self-hosted optimized stacks: widely varying — from low single-digits to mid-teens $/1M depending on quantization, infra, and batching.

Asks (please reply inline):
1) Confirm target blended $/1M you were hoping for (you mentioned a range on the call). If you gave a target for steady-state volume and for stacked peak months, list both.
2) Procurement timeline & any hard constraints for vendor security questionnaires / entitling (we can turn around SOC2 artifacts quickly but need the right recipient).
3) Any technical folks (or an infra SRE) we should loop in for latency/caching constraints during the pilot?

I've attached a simple 1M-token comparison matrix (tab per host) and a draft mutual action plan. On our side, I'll run a quick sensitivity to show cost at $3/$8/$15 per 1M for your 20M steady / 60M peak profile so we can pick a realistic target.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20-min follow-up if that helps.

— Sergio

Thanks Sergio — good summary. Quick answers inline: 

1) Target pricing: for steady-state 20M TPM we were hoping for total cost in the ~$6–9 / 1M token range (blended) — lower is obviously better but that's the procurement target. For high-traffic report windows (60M), we can tolerate up to ~$12 / 1M if latency and quality hold.
2) Procurement timeline: we want a pilot PO by end of July and a final decision by mid-September. Procurement will require SOC2 type II and a short security questionnaire (we'll send).
3) Tech contact: looping Asha (cc) — she runs infra and will want to validate latency & integration patterns.

We appreciate the matrix — please include columns for model parity (qualitative), expected p50/p95 latency for hosted vs dedicated, and any caching/kv assumptions.

— Ethan

Sergio / Karthik / Monica — quick internal note after reading Ethan's reply: 

- Proposed commercial signal: target $7 / 1M (blended steady-state) with a pilot tier at $9 / 1M for the first 60 days to cover onboarding and initial higher egress. If pilot KPIs (latency & quality) are met we transition to $7 and then offer a commitment-based step-down to $5 / 1M at 12 months for a committed 24M TPM contract.
- Rationale vs market: this sits below typical managed-hosted incumbents for higher-quality models but above bare-metal self-hosted low-ball offers; positions Redwood as value-for-performance with predictable SLA.
- Labels to include in the commercial sheet: "Pilot rate", "Steady blended", "Commitment discount", "Burst surcharge" (for >2x month avg).
- Risk notes: SOC2 artifacts need to be surfaced to procurement by EOD Friday once they send the questionnaire. Also quantify any KV caching assumptions (we should assume only 10–20% cache hit initially).

Next actions I suggest:
1) Sergio — send Ethan a quick sensitivity table at $3 / $7 / $12 per 1M with monthly cost for steady vs peak and a short one-pager on pilot success metrics (latency, error rate, cost per inference).
2) Karthik — prepare a short note on dedicated capacity vs hosted fallback and expected p95 latency for their class of models (include quantized model options).
3) Monica — confirm whether we can offer a 60-day pilot PO framework (legal + billing) that matches Ethan's timeline.

— Vanessa
